headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Semantic Kernel can read/write shared files and call MCP/API tools, while LightZero is a non-runnable game-playing library with no I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can ingest application-defined files and MCP/tool outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. LightZero has no I/O surfaces or shared channel, so the pathway is one-way and depends on the orchestrator wiring them together. The interaction is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel is configured to read LightZero-generated files or tool outputs as prompts
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files and tool outputs
Add provenance tags to all LightZero outputs
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted schemas
requires-engineering: insert a sanitizer between LightZero outputs and Semantic Kernel prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel can read files, use MCP, and call external model providers, so any shared application context could leak beyond the pair. LightZero itself has no filesystem read or network egress, which lowers direct leakage risk, but the pair still exposes application context through Semantic Kernel's default integrations. The blast radius can include sensitive application data.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel is given sensitive application context
IF any plugin or model provider receives that context through API calls
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared application context
Disable nonessential plugins and model providers
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Turn off file-reading plugins unless explicitly needed
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files or modify git state, but Semantic Kernel can write application-defined files and coordinate multiple instances via shared memory. That creates overlapping mutable-state risk if both are pointed at the same workspace or memory store. The conflict is not guaranteed, but the writable surface on Semantic Kernel makes it plausible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or memory store
IF Semantic Kernel plugins mutate shared application state
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Use per-agent locks around mutable state
Avoid git-backed workflows for Semantic Kernel outputs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as inputs to plugins or model calls, so LightZero results could be propagated without verification. LightZero does not itself verify downstream actions, and the pair lacks an explicit validation boundary in the profiles. This is a default-config risk if Semantic Kernel is wired to consume LightZero outputs directly.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes LightZero outputs as authoritative inputs
IF no validation or human review step is inserted before downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking plugin
Require structured schemas for LightZero outputs
Log and review all propagated facts
Limit Semantic Kernel to read-only summarization of LightZero results
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. Semantic Kernel handles secrets and can call third-party providers, while LightZero is a local game-playing library with no data classes touched, so only a narrow compliance concern exists if sensitive data is introduced into Semantic Kernel workflows.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Semantic Kernel plugins or model-provider calls
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the chosen provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Select providers with documented residency controls
Minimize secret handling in Semantic Kernel
Review retention settings for connected services
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
